Company: SkyHop Airlines

US regional airline (~3,500 employees) flying short domestic routes from hubs in Denver and Salt Lake City. Fleet is 60 Embraer E175 jets and 25 Airbus A320-family jets (A319 and A320). Sells tickets online and at airports, charges bag fees, and runs its own maintenance hangar. Does not fly Boeing aircraft, Airbus A220/A350, or helicopters; no cargo-only flights, no international routes.

Rules that APPLY:
- FAA airworthiness directives for Embraer E175 (ERJ 170 family) or Airbus A319/A320, and their engines
- FAA rules for airline operations, pilots, crew rest and drug/alcohol testing
- DOT consumer rules for airline passengers (refunds, fees, accessibility)
- Airspace or airport rules at Denver or Salt Lake City, and airport fees charged to passengers
- TSA security rules for airlines

Rules that DO NOT apply:
- Airworthiness directives for aircraft models we do not fly (Boeing, A220, A350, business jets, small planes, helicopters)
- Airspace changes at airports we do not serve
- Commercial space launches, drones, air-traffic-control equipment
- Banking, food, pharmacy, energy

[2026-21278] Rule — Transportation Department; Federal Aviation Administration
Title: Airworthiness Directives; Rolls-Royce Deutschland Ltd & Co KG Engines
Action: Final rule.
Abstract: The FAA is superseding Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2009-04-13 for certain Rolls-Royce Deutschland Ltd & Co KG (RRD) Model BR700- 715A1-30, BR700-715B1-30, and BR700-715C1-30 engines. AD 2009-04-13 required revising the airworthiness limitations section (ALS) of the operator's existing approved engine maintenance or inspection program, as applicable, to incorporate new or more restrictive tasks and limitations and associated thresholds and intervals for life-limited parts. AD 2009-04-13 also required removing certain low-pressure compressor (LPC) (fan) disc assemblies from service and completing the Life Limited Part Tracking Sheet. Since the FAA issued AD 2009-04-13, the manufacturer has revised the engine time limits manual (TLM) to introduce new or more restrictive tasks and limitations and associated thresholds and intervals for life-limited parts. This AD requires revising the ALS of the existing approved engine maintenance or inspection program, as applicable, to incorporate new or more restrictive tasks and limitations and associated thresholds and intervals for life-limited parts. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

[2026-21280] Notice — Federal Communications Commission
Title: Wireless Telecommunications Bureau Seeks Comment on Proposed Rebate Categories and Amounts for Radio Altimeter Retrofits To Support the Upper C-band Transition
Action: Notice; solicitation of comments.
Abstract: In this document, the Wireless Telecommunications Bureau (Bureau) invites interested parties to comment on proposed categories, dollar amounts, and any other relevant information or procedures in connection with rebates to support retrofits of radio altimeters mandated by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to facilitate the introduction of terrestrial wireless services in the Upper C-band. In Upper C-band (3.98-4.2 GHz); Expanding Flexible Use of the 3.7 to 4.2 GHz Band, GN Docket Nos. 25-59 and 18-122, Report and Order, Order of Proposed Modification, and Order on Reconsideration, FCC 26-46 (July 24, 2026) (Upper C-band R&O), the Commission established that new 3.7 GHz Service licensees will provide rebates to defined classes of eligible aircraft owners and operators to facilitate their compliance with the FAA's radio altimeter retrofit requirements and directed the Bureau to develop and seek public comment on its proposed rebate categories, dollar amounts, and other relevant procedures for administering the rebates.

[2026-21290] Rule — Transportation Department; Federal Aviation Administration
Title: Airworthiness Directives; Pratt & Whitney Division Engines
Action: Final rule.
Abstract: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Pratt & Whitney Division (PW) Model PW4052, PW4056, PW4060, PW4060A, PW4060C, PW4062, PW4062A, PW4152, PW4156, PW4156A, PW4158, PW4460, and PW4462 engines. This AD was prompted by multiple reports of tailpipe fire, loss of thrust control, and engine in-flight shutdown due to undetected deterioration of pressure burner (Pb) sensors. This AD requires replacing Pb sensors. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

Title: Clarification on Department of Justice and Department of Education Guidance Documents Regarding Federal Nondiscrimination Laws
Action: Notice; clarification.
Abstract: The U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) and U.S. Department of Education (ED) (the Departments) are issuing this document to clarify that seven guidance documents issued jointly by the Departments are not enforceable. In addition, the Departments plan to revisit these guidance documents in light of the Supreme Court's decision in Loper Bright Enters. v. Raimondo, 603 U.S. 369, 400 (2024), to assess whether they are consistent with the single best meaning of the relevant statutory text. The Departments will not rely upon these guidance documents in their enforcement of federal civil rights laws, including Titles IV and VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 (Title IV and Title VI), 42 U.S.C. 2000c et seq. and 2000d et seq., the Equal Educational Opportunities Act of 1974 (EEOA), 20 U.S.C. 1701-1720, the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 (ADA), 42 U.S.C. 12101 et seq., and Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 (Section 504), 29 U.S.C. 794.
